review_candidates.title: Systems Administrator I
review_candidates.description: About Hopscotch Primary Care At Hopscotch Primary Care, we believe great healthcare should be accessible to all people across all communities. Today, almost 20% of Americans live in a rural community, yet only 11% of physicians practice in those same communities. We are on a mission to transform healthcare in rural America. We provide high-quality primary care tailored to meet the needs of our patients through our robust care model and comprehensive care team, delivering care in our clinics, and across settings, and wrapping resources around the patients who need them most. Our patients and the care teams who serve them sit at the center of everything we do at Hopscotch. Hopscotch Primary Care takes a team approach to serve patient needs and provide the best care possible. Our goal is to provide the care each of us would want for ourselves or for our family members, in the right setting, and at the right time. Today, we are serving thousands of patients in our value-based care model and the number is growing every day. If you want to bring your experience, skill and passion to make a lasting impact in healthcare, we'd like to meet you. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Systems Administrator to join our team at a critical and exciting time for the company. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring that Hopscotch's core IT platforms are reliable, well-operated, and continuously improving as the organization scales. You will be trusted to operate independently, lead projects end-to-end, and proactively identify improvements that strengthen clinical operations, service quality, and IT system experience. RESPONSIBILITIES Near-term focus areas for this role will include, but are not limited to: Own and support the full lifecycle of core IT systems used across corporate and clinic environments. Lifecycle management of all hardware and software. Endpoint and server management, configuration, and support. Cloud platform and SaaS administration, including licensing and access governance. Identity & Access Management (IAM) administration and support across systems. Ensure systems are configured to meet security, compliance, and operational standards. Ensure the reliability, scalability, and performance of IT infrastructure through proactive improvement and automation. Monitor and improve service quality across IT systems and networks using defined metrics (e.g., Availability, performance, incident trends, etc). Identify recurring operational issues and drive corrective actions within assigned systems, through change management and improvements. Drive infrastructure efficiency and performance within assigned systems, including design, implementation, and ongoing iteration. Design and build internal tools and automations to solve operational needs (e.g., AI agents, Foundry pipelines, Azure Playbooks). Maintain clear, consistent, and well-documented IT standards that support scale, security, and operational reality. Contribute to the creation, review, and implementation of IT policies and procedures. Support disaster recovery and business continuity planning, testing, and implementation. Ensure system changes are implemented thoughtfully and consistently to reduce variance, risk, and configuration drift. Provide high-quality technical support while continuously improving service delivery and user experience. Serve as the escalation point for complex or high-impact technical issues. Own the quality, accuracy, and usefulness of IT ticket data. Use operational signals (ticket trends, response times, failure patterns) to inform prioritization and drive improvements. Propose and implement improvements to support workflows based on measured impact and feedback. ABOUT YOU: Business-oriented with the ability to articulate business needs, scope solutions and clearly communicate value and timing of work. Data-informed and decisive - confident making prioritization decisions using a mix of qualitative insights, quantitative data, KPIs and expected business impact. A clear and compelling communicator ; able to articulate the strategy and value of the tactical roadmap items to audiences ranging from technical peers to executive leadership. Self-aware and resilient , able to recognize missteps, learn from execution failures and re-engage with confidence and a bias toward action. From a cultural perspective, you are: Accountable . You hold a high standard and you expect it from others too. Someone who treats mistakes as data. You move fast, name what isn't working, fix it, and carry the lesson forward. Customer-obsessed. You build genuine empathy with users, dig into what they actually need, and stay focused on solving real problems. A problem-solver, not a finger-pointer. You own challenges alongside your teammates - no blame, no deflection, just shared accountability for finding the way forward. A contributor who shapes the answer. You bring your strengths and perspective to every conversation because rigorous debate is how the strongest solutions get built. Comfortable with uncertainty. The plan will change and the priorities will shift - you make smart calls with what you have and course-correct with good judgement when things evolve. QUALIFICATIONS: 2+ years of IT / Helpdesk / system administration experience Bachelor's degree (computer science, engineering or technical discipline) A degree is not required; we heavily encourage you to apply regardless of college experience. Experience in maintaining troubleshooting a wide variety of systems and networks. Preferred: Experience with Identity & Endpoint management for both Mac and Windows. Experience with Network management and tooling (e.g., VLAN/WLAN) Experience with cybersecurity principles (CIA) Experience with AI tooling such as Claude (Code), ChatGPT (Codex), and/or similar tools. Comp TIA Network+ Certification Security + Certification At Hopscotch Primary Care, we embrace diversity, invest in a culture of inclusion and positivity and encourage all to apply to join our team. You will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

This role requires strong engineering judgment, the ability to execute technically complex work end‑to‑end, and comfort operating in highly regulated, large‑scale enterprise environments. The Senior Infrastructure Engineer plays a critical role in modernizing McKesson’s infrastructure, accelerating cloud adoption, improving platform reliability, reducing technical debt, and delivering tangible business value across the organization. Infrastructure Strategy & Design: Plan, design, and implement migration initiatives across on‑premises, hybrid, and Azure cloud environments. Architect scalable, resilient, and secure infrastructure solutions aligned with McKesson enterprise standards. Evaluate legacy infrastructure and define modernization and migration strategies that support business objectives. Migration Execution & Delivery: Deliver migration plans that achieve documented performance improvements, availability enhancements, or cost savings. Participate in change reviews, implementation planning, and post‑implementation validation to confirm changes meet technical, operational, and business requirements. Collaborate with compute, network, storage, operations, and cybersecurity teams to ensure end‑to‑end solution integrity and operational readiness. Advanced proficiency in PowerShell scripting to automate infrastructure provisioning, configuration, migration activities, and ongoing operational tasks. Strong working knowledge of application architecture and deployment processes, with the ability to align infrastructure design and implementation to application and business requirements. Implement and maintain monitoring and alerting capabilities to ensure the ongoing health, availability, and performance of services.
